classification: READ-ONLY source audit; no code/tests/CI/provisioning performed; existing tests below are source references only
main_conclusion: Final user/implicit ROW mutations share final range admission; physical index updates are dependent local apply, while audit/sync/broker outboxes and memory-index jobs have distinct local persistence. Replicated row correctness is not proof of queue/audit/worker migration or quorum durability.

findings.topic: Final row footprint and internal row writes
findings.behavior: spatial_paged commit repairs final writes, injects flashback history, builds index mutations, then builds admission mutations from every actual tx.write; coordinator hashes collection+record_id and rejects multiple ranges before WAL. No origin-range locality override is present for flashback history or workflow receipt rows. This proves possible explicit rejection, not a demonstrated lost or partially committed transaction.

findings.classification: implemented local durability; distributed scope gap
findings.behavior: Record-audit events, SyncOps and PendingBrokerPublish are not extra tx.write records and are not independently hashed. They are encoded as distinct TxFrames before the same local Commit decision. Post-durable publication is idempotent or fences for verified recovery; local checkpoint/outbox tests exist. RangeWriteCommand contains admitted row mutations only, with no broker/record-audit/sync sidecar field. Native replica projection suppresses newly generated record audits/sync ops. There is no basis to claim original audit/outbox IDs or broker queue state migrate or survive quorum failover solely because all row mutations do. No loss experiment was run.

findings.topic: Registered and Joined physical image rows
findings.behavior: Both actual row producers explicitly bypass a second logical range admission under genuine original native scope, require imported_projection=true and enqueue_memory_jobs_on_commit=false, and use ordinary row/index apply plus native Tx/WAL custody. They suppress fresh model/embedding jobs and newly generated record-audit/sync output; they are not copying the source local broker state, sync.log or event segment. Spatial index-maintenance events may still be locally appended; do not describe projection as producing zero local events.

Indexes/FTS postings are dependent physical state updated by the normal transaction apply on installed definitions, not separately hashed logical rows. Paged read-through postings are maintained in paged apply; resident BTree/FTS/JSONB/array state in apply_index_mutations. The source manifest/target receipt pins schema, reader features, namespace identities and index definitions. The independent target verifier explicitly marks independent_index_parity=false; copied primary rows/definition equality do not certify actual posting/query parity, global uniqueness, FTS scoring, rebuild/asset migration or whole-cluster DDL.

findings.classification: implemented local worker persistence; migration unqualified
findings.behavior: Memory-index jobs are held in local memory_index_jobs and persisted to memory-index-jobs.json, not a distributed record namespace. Normal native command/historical projections set imported_projection=true but do not disable the default enqueue_memory_jobs_on_commit=true; their explicit finalizer can enqueue/process local index jobs when configured. This is local maintenance, not proof of duplicate business execution. Registered/Joined image producers disable it. Workflow enqueue_on_commit is different: it writes a real job receipt row plus buffers a local broker publication; its receipt key joins final range admission, while its broker payload remains a WAL sidecar. No transparent global worker/lease/receipt migration is established.

Bounded range snapshots scan every pinned paged collection at an MVCC snapshot, emit only records whose own collection+ID token belongs to the selected range, and carry reader requirements. This includes any internal collections as independent rows, not files/segments/worker memory. The generic CommitFrame range filter keeps only matching writes, preserves continuity, and explicitly REJECTS a nonempty whole-database origin journal; it does not silently filter journals. Native historical/range command replay reconstructs admitted rows from the command spine with imported_projection, not whole source TxFrame outboxes. Old unscoped/generic relocation paths are separately gated on born-native databases; do not generalize their behavior to guarded native import.

findings.topic: Legacy whole-database streaming versus range replication
findings.behavior: The whole-database CommitFrame exporter includes original audit journal only when record_journal is enabled; retained original envelopes/signatures have dedicated tests. It explicitly ignores TxFrame::BrokerPublish and SyncOps when constructing stream frames. Whole-database importer passes empty broker and sync arrays into its local WAL encoder while carrying the optional original journal. Therefore native single-primary streaming row/journal guarantees must not be promoted into broker queue or original sync-op identity replication. Whole-file HA/backup is a different contract.
